fig1_extensive_scaling.svg: What makes a property *extensive*: double the system and you double the property. Volume, internal energy and kinetic energy carry different units and magnitudes, so each is divided by its own one-unit value (scales_with_extent) — and all three then land exactly on the line $X(k)/X(1)=k$. The collapse is the content of the definition: an extensive property has no meaning without saying how much substance there is. Contrast module 1.4, where the same rescaling leaves the intensive properties flat at 1.
fig2_additivity.svg: The operational test for extensivity (is_additive): cut the system into parts, evaluate the property on each, and check that the pieces sum to the whole. Three subsystems of the same substance ($v=0.8$ m$^3$/kg) holding 3, 5 and 2 kg contribute 2.4, 4.0 and 1.6 m$^3$, summing exactly to the 8.0 m$^3$ of the combined 10 kg system. Mass, volume, energy and entropy all pass this test; temperature and pressure do not, which is precisely why they are classified as intensive instead.
